reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Jay has to draw a shape.
- It must have 5 sides.
- It must have one line of symmetry.
Jay has started to draw the shape.
Complete Jay’s shape.

[Image: an incomplete shape with three sides forming a rectangle on a grid.]

descriptors:
Correct shape drawn which has 5 sides and 1 line of symmetry. The new vertex must be within ±2 mm of the line of symmetry (accept the new vertex anywhere on the line of symmetry, provided there are 5 sides).
[Image: figure drawn on grid with three lines forming an incomplete rectangle on the bottom. Two lines drawn on top to close the figure and form a convex interior angle.] OR
[Image: figure drawn on grid with three lines forming an incomplete rectangle on the bottom. Two lines sloping inwards are drawn on top to close the figure and form a convex interior angle.]

[Image: figure drawn on grid with three lines forming an incomplete rectangle on the bottom. The rectangle is completed with a fourth line and then two additional lines are drawn on top to close the figure and form a convex interior angle.]
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Geometry Tiles
Instruction:

For this item, you have been given a piece of cardboard with 6 tiles like the ones shown below. Take the piece of cardboard, and punch out the 6 tiles.

If you do not have the piece of cardboard, raise your hand.

4 Triangle Tiles
[Image: Four triangle tiles]

2 Trapezoid Tiles
[Image: Two trapezoid tiles]

These tiles can be used to make new figures. One problem has been done for you

USE: 3 Triangle Tiles
MAKE: A trapezoid
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.
[Image: Example showing a trapezoid drawn on the grid]

Now try these problems.

B.

USE: 2 Trapezoid Tiles
MAKE: A 6-sided figure
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.

[Image: Triangular grid]

descriptors:
Makes a correct 6-sided figure, e.g., one of those shown below (in any orientation).
[Image: Five sample 6-sided figures each made from two trapezoid tiles: a regular hexagon joined at the long bases; an hourglass shape joined at the short bases; an L-shaped figure joined along legs; an offset hexagon joined partially along long bases; and another 6-sided figure joined along legs]
Incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)
Blank

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem includes four diagrams:
1. '4 Triangle Tiles': Four identical equilateral triangles of unit side length, arranged in a row pointing alternately up, down, up, and down.
2. '2 Trapezoid Tiles': Two identical isosceles trapezoids each composed of three equilateral triangle units (bottom base 2 units, top base 1 unit, legs 1 unit for the first one; and inverted with top base 2 units, bottom base 1 unit for the second one).
3. Worked example grid: An isometric grid forming a parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides of 3 units each and slanted sides of 2 units each, divided by dashed lines into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangles. In the top-right portion, a trapezoid made of 3 triangle units (top side 1 unit, bottom side 2 units, slanted sides 1 unit) is outlined in bold solid lines.
4. Part B response grid: An identical empty parallelogram-shaped isometric grid with top and bottom edges of 3 units, slanted sides of 2 units, divided into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangle units by dashed lines.

reference_items.figure_description:
A square grid containing six outlined shapes labeled A through F:
- Shape A: A square measuring 3 units by 3 units.
- Shape B: An irregular stepped polygon with horizontal and vertical edges of varying lengths (not 4 sides, sides of different lengths).
- Shape C: A vertical rectangle measuring 2 units wide and 5 units tall.
- Shape D: A symmetrical 12-sided cross (plus sign) shape composed of five 2-by-2 square sections; every side is 2 units long.
- Shape E: An isosceles trapezoid with a horizontal top base of 4 units, a horizontal bottom base of 6 units, and a height of 4 units.
- Shape F: A square oriented as a rhombus/diamond with horizontal and vertical diagonals measuring 4 units; all 4 sides are of equal length.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
